result.keywords: AbstractOutdoor visible light sensor networks combine communication, sensing, and environmental exposure in scenarios such as street lighting, vehicle links, and smart-city monitoring. Compared with indoor deployments, these systems face higher interference, variable illumination, weather-driven attenuation, and stronger security risks due to open-channel operation. This article proposes a hybrid authentication and key agreement framework tailored to outdoor VLC-enabled sensor networks. The scheme integrates lightweight mutual authentication, replay resistance, device compromise mitigation, and traceability protection while preserving low communication and computational overhead. Formal verification is provided using ProVerif, and performance is assessed against related protocols in terms of message complexity, storage cost, and security properties. The study also discusses deployment considerations for fog, rain, haze, and solar-powered receivers, and identifies research opportunities for resilient Li-Fi based sensing infrastructures.
result.title: A hybrid authentication framework for outdoor visible light sensor networks
